name: Black fianchetto (g7 bishop, or its b7 file-mirror)

plans.label: Open the long diagonal
plans.description: Trade or lever away the central pawns in the bishop's path so the fianchetto bishop reaches across the board at full length.

success.note: The fianchetto bishop stands on its home diagonal with every intervening square empty. The file-mirrored arm is kept deliberately: this entry's own trigger is an any[] whose second arm is the same file mirror, so the entry admits a b6/b7 queenside fianchetto and a plan signature that did not mirror could never be satisfied there. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-16 with `make expression-census` over 827 authored spine positions across 56 packs; the 2026-08-15 reading below it (694 positions, trigger 44, mirror 0, g7-d4 clear 0) is SUPERSEDED and two of its three headline numbers are now false. The trigger fires 95 times across ten packs: 85 through the unmirrored g6/g7 arm and 10 through the file mirror, in london-wedge-black-counterplay (2) and nimzo-doubled-c-pawns (8). The mirrored arm's 2026-08-15 zero was recorded as a coverage fact rather than a defect, and the corpus has since supplied the coverage - so the arm D76 called 'from the wrong side of the board' is now exercised by authored content. The clear-diagonal half, walked segment by segment over the 86 positions holding a bishop on g7: g7-f6 clear fires 86, g7-e5 clear 23, g7-d4 clear 5, and g7-c3, g7-b2 and g7-a1 all fire 0. The wall is therefore the d4 square, not the e5 square the earlier reading stopped at. Of the 5 positions that reach d4, 2 have a white PAWN on d4 (grunfeld-exchange-fianchetto) and 3 have a white KNIGHT there (maroczy-bind-white-squeeze); none has it empty. That is a limit on this plan's own prose, recorded rather than papered over: in 3 of the 5 closest positions the obstruction is a piece, and 'trade or lever away the central pawns' does not describe how to remove it. Both signature arms - g7-a1 clear, and its b7-h1 file mirror - still fire 0 of 827; satisfiability is settled by the two anchored witnesses in content/witnesses/expression-witnesses.json, not by corpus coverage.

plans.label: Guard the king's dark squares
plans.description: The bishop is also the king's roof: before any trade of it, arrange which piece inherits the dark squares around the king.

success.note: Whether the remaining pieces can re-guard the dark squares is not pawn arithmetic.

plans.label: Trade the fianchetto bishop
plans.description: Exchange the dark-squared bishops to soften the squares the g6 pawn no longer guards, the standard prelude to a kingside attack.

success.note: The fianchetto pawn still stands and the bishop that lived behind it is off the board. The earlier note declined this as undecidable; it was wrong about the vocabulary. A bishop can never change shade, so bishop_on_shade distinguishes a bishop that was traded from one that merely moved away, which pieceOnSquare cannot. The mirrored arm covers the queenside fianchetto the trigger also admits, where the bishop is the light-squared one.

plans.label: Lever the wing pawn
plans.description: March the outside pawn to strike the fianchetto pawn and open that wing's outside file for the heavy pieces.

success.note: The outside file is open or half-open for White while the adjacent fianchetto pawn still marks the target.

watch: Every trade that involves the fianchetto bishop.
Whether the long diagonal is open, blocked by a pawn, or blocked by a defended piece.
The outside pawn's licence to run: cheap when the kings sit on opposite wings, committal when they share one.
typicalMistakes: Giving up the g7 bishop without counting who guards the king's dark squares afterwards.
Blocking the long diagonal with an own pawn that can never advance again.
Launching the h-pawn while the centre is still fluid enough to open against the attacker.

sources: UNGROUNDED: agent-authored strategic claims with no citation, engine evaluation, corpus frequency, or owner review; fianchetto doctrine rendered from model knowledge.

Trigger scope: this entry covers Black fianchettos on g7 and their files-mirrored b7 form. White g2/b2 forms require separately authored entries because colour mirroring changes which side owns every plan. The trigger still stops matching when the bishop leaves its home square even though the pawn structure may persist.
